job.title: Senior Manufacturing Engineer – Process Planning & CAD
job.description:
Salary: £50,000 – £55,000 depending on experience
Location: Aylesbury

Aerospace Precision Engineering | Gibbs Gears Precision Engineers Ltd | Aylesbury

Gibbs Gears Precision Engineers Ltd is a specialist aerospace and precision engineering business, manufacturing high-accuracy gears, splines, shafts and complex transmission components for demanding customers in aerospace, defence and high-performance engineering sectors.

We are looking for an experienced Senior Manufacturing Engineer / Production Engineer to support the development and industrialisation of new and existing components. This is a key role within our Engineering team, focused on turning complex customer drawings into practical, controlled and repeatable manufacturing processes.

The Role
The successful candidate will be responsible for reviewing customer drawings, developing manufacturing routes, creating stage drawings and CAD models, defining tooling and workholding requirements, and supporting production through NPI and first manufacture.
In simple terms, this role works out how we are going to make the part and ensures the shop floor has the correct engineering information to manufacture it successfully.

Key Responsibilities
  • Interpret complex aerospace engineering drawings, specifications, GD&T, material requirements and special process requirements.
  • Develop manufacturing routes and operation sequences for precision machined components.
  • Support Production Readiness Studies and identify technical, quality and process risks before release to production.
  • Create and maintain stage drawings, manufacturing drawings and 3D CAD models.
  • Define tooling, workholding, fixtures, gauges, consumables and outside process requirements.
  • Support CNC turning, milling, gear cutting, gear grinding, heat treatment, plating and inspection process planning.
  • Work closely with Engineering, Production, Quality, Planning and Purchasing to ensure jobs are production-ready.
  • Support NPI, first-off manufacture, process prove-out and continuous improvement activities.
  • Maintain accurate manufacturing data within the ERP system.

The Ideal Candidate
We are looking for someone with a strong manufacturing engineering background, ideally gained within aerospace, defence, motorsport, gears, transmission components or high-precision machining.
You should have:
  • Strong ability to read and interpret complex engineering drawings and GD&T.
  • Good understanding of CNC turning, milling and precision machining processes.
  • Experience creating manufacturing routes, process plans and stage drawings.
  • CAD experience, ideally SolidWorks.
  • Knowledge of tooling, fixtures, workholding, gauges and manufacturing consumables.
  • Awareness of special processes such as heat treatment, plating and subcontract operations.
  • Good spreadsheet, ERP/MRP and project tracking skills.
  • A practical, hands-on engineering mindset with strong problem-solving ability.
Experience with gear cutting, gear grinding or aerospace FAIR / AS9100 environments would be a strong advantage.

Why Join Gibbs Gears?
This is an opportunity to join a growing aerospace precision engineering business with strong technical capability, significant investment in machinery and systems, and a clear focus on developing robust, repeatable manufacturing processes.
The role will suit someone who enjoys being close to the product, the process and the shop floor — not just working behind a desk.

£50,000 – £55,000 depending on experience

job.title: Project Engineer – Aerospace Industrialisation
job.description:
Location: Aylesbury
Company: Gibbs Gears Precision Engineers Ltd
Salary: £34,000 – £42,000 depending on experience

Job Type: Full-time, permanent
Gibbs Gears Precision Engineers Ltd is a specialist aerospace and precision engineering business, manufacturing high-accuracy gears, splines, shafts and complex machined components for customers in aerospace, defence and high-performance engineering sectors.

We are looking for a motivated and organised Project Engineer – Aerospace Industrialisation to support the delivery of aerospace and precision component projects from order launch through to successful production release.

This role is suited to someone with an engineering or manufacturing background who wants to develop their career in technical project management, NPI and aerospace industrialisation.

The Role
The successful candidate will act as a central point of coordination for assigned projects, working closely with customers, suppliers and internal teams to ensure project actions, timings, risks and deliverables are clearly managed.

This is not a purely administrative role. The successful candidate will need to understand engineering and manufacturing environments, be comfortable working with technical information, and be confident chasing actions through to completion.

The focus of the role is simple:
Track, coordinate, communicate, escalate and deliver.

Key Responsibilities
  • Support the coordination and delivery of aerospace and precision component projects.
  • Maintain project timing plans, action trackers, risk registers and status reports.
  • Track key deliverables including materials, tooling, fixtures, gauges, documentation, outside processes, engineering actions and production readiness requirements.
  • Coordinate with Engineering, Quality, Production, Planning, Purchasing and Supply Chain to keep projects moving.
  • Liaise with customers and suppliers to support clear communication, updates and action closure.
  • Attend and support project launch meetings, engineering reviews, production readiness reviews and customer progress meetings.
  • Follow up open actions and ensure owners are clear on responsibilities and deadlines.
  • Identify risks, delays and blockers early, and escalate issues before they impact customer commitments.
  • Support coordination of raw material, heat treatment, plating, coating and subcontract operations.
  • Maintain accurate project information using spreadsheets, trackers, ERP/MRP systems and internal project tools.
  • Help ensure new parts transition from engineering launch into production in a controlled and organised way.

The Ideal Candidate
We are looking for someone who is organised, proactive and confident at driving actions through to completion.

You should have:
  • Experience supporting or coordinating engineering, manufacturing, NPI, industrialisation or customer projects.
  • A background or strong interest in aerospace, precision engineering or complex manufactured components.
  • Ability to read and understand engineering drawings, tolerances and technical requirements.
  • Good understanding of manufacturing environments and cross-functional project delivery.
  • Strong follow-up discipline — someone who does not just record actions, but helps make sure they are closed.
  • Clear communication skills with customers, suppliers and internal teams.
  • The confidence to ask questions, challenge progress and escalate issues early.
  • Good spreadsheet, tracker and reporting skills.
  • Experience using ERP/MRP or project tracking systems would be beneficial.
  • A structured, hands-on approach with strong attention to detail.

Desirable Experience
Experience in any of the following would be beneficial:
  • Coordinating engineering, NPI, industrialisation or manufacturing projects from launch through to completion.
  • Managing project deliverables across engineering, quality, production, purchasing, planning and supply chain.
  • Preparing and communicating clear project updates for customers, suppliers and internal stakeholders.
  • Supporting project launch reviews, production readiness reviews, gate reviews or customer progress meetings.
  • Coordinating material, tooling, gauges, fixtures, documentation, outside processes and approval activities against a project plan.
  • Working in a controlled manufacturing environment where deadlines, customer communication, traceability and documentation are important.
  • Exposure to CNC machining, turning, milling, grinding, gear cutting, gear grinding or complex machined components.
  • Exposure to AS9100, FAIR, PPAP, ISIR, NPI or production readiness processes.
  • Project management training or qualifications such as APM, PRINCE2, PMP or similar would be beneficial, but practical project delivery experience is more important.

Key Skills
  • Project coordination
  • Action tracking and follow-up
  • Risk and issue management
  • Customer and supplier communication
  • Engineering awareness
  • Drawing interpretation
  • Manufacturing process awareness
  • Production readiness support
  • Supply chain coordination
  • Spreadsheet and status reporting
  • ERP/MRP awareness
  • Clear written and verbal communication

﻿Why Join Gibbs Gears?
This is an opportunity to join a growing aerospace precision engineering business with strong technical capability, continued investment in machinery and systems, and a clear focus on improving project delivery, production readiness and customer communication.
The role will suit someone who enjoys being close to the product, the customer and the manufacturing process, and who wants to grow into a stronger project engineering / industrialisation role within aerospace precision manufacturing.

job.title: CNC Turner Setter / Operator
job.description:
CNC Turner Setter / Operator

Location: Stoke Mandeville, Aylesbury, Buckinghamshire
Shift: Early Shift – Monday to Friday, 6:00am – 2:00pm
Salary: Competitive DOE + Overtime

About Gibbs Gears
Gibbs Gears is a high-precision engineering company specialising in the manufacture of gears, shafts, transmissions and complex machined components for sectors including aerospace, Formula 1, motorsport, medical and advanced engineering. Gibbs operate a modern CNC machining environment with ongoing investment in advanced turning technology, including Doosan and Mazak multi-axis turning centres.

The Role
We are looking for an experienced CNC Turner Setter / Operator to join our precision machining team on an early shift.
The role will involve setting and operating modern CNC turning centres producing complex precision components to tight tolerances in a high-specification engineering environment.
This is a hands-on role suited to someone with a strong CNC turning background who is confident setting tools, offsets, proving out jobs and maintaining machining quality independently.

Responsibilities
  • Setting and operating CNC turning centres
  • Working on Doosan Puma / Lynx and Fanuc turning machines
  • Setting tool offsets and wear offsets
  • Producing precision components to tight tolerances
  • Reading and working from engineering drawings
  • Proving out jobs and making program edits where required
  • Monitoring tooling and machining quality
  • Conducting self-inspection using measuring equipment
  • Troubleshooting machining issues and supporting continuous improvement
  • Maintaining safe and organised working practices

Candidate Requirements
  • Experience as a CNC Turner Setter / Operator
  • Strong CNC lathe / turning centre background
  • Experience with Fanuc controls (or similar)
  • Ability to set tools and offsets independently
  • Experience machining precision components
  • Able to work from engineering drawings and inspection equipment
  • Good understanding of tooling, speeds and feeds

Highly Desirable
Experience with:
  • Doosan Puma / Lynx machines / Nakumara
  • Y-axis / live tooling
  • Twin spindle lathes
  • Aerospace / motorsport / precision engineering environments
  • Low-volume high-precision machining

Benefits
  • Competitive hourly rate depending on experience
  • Overtime available at enhanced rates
  • 28 days holiday including bank holidays
  • Pension scheme
  • Ongoing training and development
  • Modern CNC machining environment
  • Team lunches and company events
  • Free parking and refreshments

﻿Please apply now if you are interested or have any questions and we will be in touch.

job.title: Senior CNC Turner (Mazatrol) – Late Shift
job.description:
Senior CNC Turner (Mazatrol) – Late Shift

Location: Witham, Essex
Shift: Monday–Thursday, Late Shift (4 days)
Salary: £25p/h (including late shift premium)

About Copsey Engineering
Copsey Engineering is a well-established precision engineering company producing high-tolerance components across a wide range of materials for sectors including aerospace, defence, motorsport, marine, automotive and medical. We are a small, close-knit team with a strong focus on quality, craftsmanship and reliability.

The Role
We’re looking for a highly capable CNC Turner with strong Mazatrol experience to join our late shift team. This is a hands-on role suited to an experienced machinist who can work independently from engineering drawings, programme and set their own jobs, and take real ownership of quality and output.
This is a role for an ambitious, hands-on CNC Turner who takes pride in their work and has the drive to grow. Alongside programming, setting and running jobs independently, the position offers the opportunity over time to take on greater responsibility supporting the Manufacturing Manager, helping guide less experienced operators, and developing into a broader production and leadership role as the business continues to grow.

Key Responsibilities
  • Programme, set and operate CNC lathes using Mazatrol
  • Work from engineering drawings to produce precision components to tight tolerances
  • Plan setups, select tooling and machine small batch and one-off components
  • Work independently on late shift with minimal supervision
  • Carry out self-inspection using manual inspection equipment (CMM experience beneficial)
  • Work to high-quality standards within a precision engineering environment (AS9100 experience advantageous)
  • Maintain high standards of quality, accuracy and housekeeping
  • Support the team where needed and share knowledge with less experienced operators

Skills & Experience
  • Strong background in CNC turning with Mazatrol programming essential
  • Good understanding of engineering drawings and GD&T
  • Confident setting, proving out and running jobs independently
  • Experience producing high-precision components across a range of materials
  • Milling knowledge an advantage but not essential
  • A practical, reliable approach with pride in workmanship

Personal Qualities
  • Self-motivated and dependable
  • Comfortable working independently on a late shift
  • Positive attitude with a willingness to get stuck in
  • Ambitious, with the drive and “fire in the belly” to grow with the business over time

Opportunity
This role would suit an experienced CNC Turner looking for a stable, long-term position within a small team where their skill and experience are valued. For the right person, there is scope to develop into a broader role supporting production, mentoring others, and progressing into greater responsibility within the manufacturing team.
